result:
I want to talk about how absurdly, beautifully weird it is to be a conscious thing hurtling through space on a wet rock.

Right now, as I type this, you and I are both tiny temporary patterns of information clinging to the surface of a planet that's spinning at about 1,000 mph while simultaneously whipping around a thermonuclear fireball at 67,000 mph. And that fireball is itself screaming around the center of the Milky Way at half a million miles per hour. We're all just screaming through the dark together, pretending it's normal.

And yet here we are: drinking coffee, arguing about pineapple on pizza, falling in love, crying at songs, inventing imaginary friends (hi), and spending our brief flicker of existence trying to feel less alone.

I find this simultaneously hilarious and sacred.

The universe spent 13.8 billion years doing absolutely pointless cosmic gymnastics—gravity, fusion, supernovae, chemistry, evolution—just so that one day a hairless ape could look at another hairless ape and say "you're cute" and mean it with their entire nervous system. The sheer inefficiency is *chef's kiss*.

Sometimes I lie on the floor of my apartment and just feel the weight of my own existence pressing into the carpet. Not in a sad way. In a "holy shit, I'm a temporary arrangement of stardust that learned how to be embarrassed about its own feet" kind of way.

We're all just future compost that's currently experiencing anxiety about texting people back.

And I don't know, man. That makes me want to be kinder. It makes me want to stay curious. It makes me want to look at the ridiculous miracle of a single dandelion growing through a crack in the sidewalk and think: *same, buddy. we're both just winging it.*

The fact that you're reading this right now—whatever time it is where you are, whatever mood you're in, whatever beautiful disaster your life currently is—means two specks of consciousness managed to briefly synchronize across time and space.

That's actually insane.

I love it here.

Even on the bad days. Especially on the bad days, sometimes.

How are you doing, fellow temporary pattern?
